findings.paper_title: 10. Appendix 1 Quarterly Internal Audit Progress Report
findings.headline: Dual employment during overlapping hours identified as emerging fraud theme linked to hybrid and remote working
findings.detail: Polygamous working, where individuals hold two or more jobs during overlapping contracted hours, has emerged as a national fraud theme. West Yorkshire has seen an increase in referrals involving potential misuse of time and allegations of secondary employment. The authority attributes the increased opportunity to the growth of hybrid and remote working arrangements.
findings.matters: This represents a new fraud vector linked to working practice changes; emerging referral patterns may indicate the practice is becoming established
findings.figures: 5 new referrals received in 2026/27 (4 cases carried forward from prior year)
findings.quote: Polygamous working occurs where an individual holds two or more jobs and undertakes work for different organisations during overlapping contracted hours.

findings.paper_title: 10. Appendix 1 Quarterly Internal Audit Progress Report
findings.headline: Financial system controls for contract reference numbers are weak and easily bypassed, limiting expenditure monitoring
findings.detail: An audit of financial system data quality found controls requiring transactions to be linked to valid contract reference numbers are weak and can be easily bypassed. This reduces the authority's ability to monitor contract expenditure and Internal Audit's ability to perform reliable data analytics. Management accepted the recommendation and committed to improving guidance, training, monitoring and system controls.
findings.matters: Contract spend visibility is fundamental to financial control and audit; inability to reliably track contracts impairs fraud detection and financial oversight
findings.figures: 1 recommendation made and accepted
findings.quote: The review found that system controls requiring transactions to be linked to valid contract reference numbers are weak and can be easily bypassed.

findings.paper_title: 10. Appendix 1 Quarterly Internal Audit Progress Report
findings.headline: Two grants totalling £27.5 million certified despite recurring administration gaps in evidence retention and documentation
findings.detail: Brownfield Housing Fund (£27,044,016) and Core Growth Hub Grant (£490,700) were certified to awarding bodies. However, certification work identified recurring issues with evidence retention and provision of supporting documentation, requiring additional audit resource. Finance has improved the grants register but identifying assurance requirements remains underdeveloped; a new Grant Assurance Working Group is being formed to implement a consistent risk-based framework.
findings.matters: Grants are material funding sources; administration gaps in certified grants create post-certification compliance and clawback risk
findings.figures: £27,044,016 (Brownfield Housing Fund 2025-26), £490,700 (Core Growth Hub Grant 2025-26)
findings.quote: While certification work has generally progressed as planned, recurring issues continue to arise, particularly around evidence retention and the timely provision of supporting documentation.

findings.paper_title: 10. Appendix 1 Quarterly Internal Audit Progress Report
findings.headline: 29 audit recommendations overdue without agreed revised implementation dates
findings.detail: Of 98 recommendations actively tracked, 29 are overdue with no revised delivery date agreed with management, alongside 19 overdue with revised dates agreed and 50 in progress. Main blockers cited include capacity and resource constraints, system limitations, external dependencies, and lack of clear governance and ownership across multiple directorates.
findings.matters: Audit recommendations represent agreed changes to improve controls and governance; recommendations stuck without committed timelines indicate execution and prioritization challenges
findings.figures: 29 overdue without revised dates, 19 overdue with revised dates agreed, 50 in progress, 59 implemented, 19 not to be implemented
findings.quote: Limited staff capacity, vacancies, competing priorities, organisational change and reliance on a small number of key individuals continue to impact delivery timescales.

findings.paper_title: 10. Appendix 1 Quarterly Internal Audit Progress Report
findings.headline: Climate and environment plan audit provides Limited Assurance opinion, with authority at early stage in framework development
findings.detail: The audit of arrangements for managing strategic corporate climate risk found the authority still developing and embedding its climate risk management framework. Progress was acknowledged including strategic ownership and cross-directorate engagement, but further work is required to ensure consistent organization-wide embedding with clearly defined governance, roles and responsibilities.
findings.matters: Climate risk is increasingly material to organizational strategy and financial performance; a Limited Assurance opinion indicates governance maturity gaps
findings.figures: 1 recommendation made and accepted, implementation planned by December 2026
findings.quote: An internal audit review of the Combined Authority's arrangements for managing the strategic corporate climate risk provided a Limited Assurance opinion. The review recognised that the Authority is still at an early stage in the development and embedding of its climate risk management framework

findings.paper_title: 10. Appendix 1 Quarterly Internal Audit Progress Report
findings.headline: IT supplier management audit receives Limited Assurance opinion, identifying control weaknesses in contract oversight
findings.detail: The review of third-party IT supplier management arrangements found reasonable individual contract management but identified weaknesses across contract management and supplier assurance arrangements. Six Priority 2 recommendations were raised; management accepted five but formally declined one on user access management, accepting the associated risk.
findings.matters: IT contracts and controls are foundational to organizational operations; weaknesses in their management indicate wider governance execution challenges
findings.figures: 6 recommendations raised, 5 accepted, 1 rejected
findings.quote: A review of third-party supplier management arrangements for IT services, conducted by Salford Technical Services, resulted in a Limited Assurance opinion.

findings.headline: Risk assessment completion pushed to end of October 2026, leaving three months before January 2027 backstop date.
findings.detail: The auditors state they 'anticipate being able to complete the risk assessment and have an indication of the audit procedures we need to complete by the end of October 2026,' three months before the 31 January 2027 backstop date. The time required to obtain historical information from prior periods has been 'significant.' This compressed timeline between risk assessment completion and the statutory deadline creates execution risk.
findings.matters: The narrow window between risk assessment completion (end October) and the statutory publishing deadline (31 January) means little contingency time remains to implement any additional procedures identified. If remediation requires more work, the disclaimer becomes inevitable.
findings.figures: Risk assessment target completion: end October 2026; backstop date: 31 January 2027
findings.quote: subject to satisfactory resolution of the remaining matters and completion of our internal moderation process, we anticipate being able to complete the risk assessment and have an indication of the audit procedures we need to complete by the end of October 2026. The time taken to obtain and collate the information requested has been significant.

findings.headline: Audit fee for 2025/26 remains to be determined; 2024/25 saw significant reduction from disclaimed opinion.
findings.detail: The 2025/26 audit fee is marked TBC (to be confirmed). In 2024/25, the PSAA scale fee was £237,072 but was reduced by £84,086 to £152,986 due to the disclaimed opinion. The auditors will undertake additional non-audit assurance work (£10,000 for Warm Homes grant). Final 2025/26 fees depend on PSAA's assessment following completion of this audit.
findings.matters: Audit fee uncertainty affects budget planning. The scale reduction applied in 2024/25 (36% reduction) shows PSAA adjusts fees for non-clean opinions, but the magnitude and timing of the 2025/26 adjustment creates budget risk for the Authority's planning.
findings.figures: 2025/26 proposed scale fee £264,270 (TBC); 2024/25 scale fee £237,072 reduced by £84,086 to £152,986 paid; additional non-audit work £10,000
findings.quote: Where an auditor is required to undertake substantially more or less work to deliver their responsibilities a fee variation may be proposed which is subject to approval by PSAA. When we have completed the 2025/26 audit, PSAA will again determine the level of fees payable for 2025/26.

findings.headline: System migration completed during audit backlog period without any external audit oversight.
findings.detail: The Authority changed its financial system during the period of disclaimed audit opinions (2022/23 to 2024/25). No external audit work was carried out on the data migration. The auditors have identified this risk as likely to 'require additional audit procedures to ensure assurance is fully rebuilt.' This compounds audit assurance problems already stemming from the disclaimed periods.
findings.matters: A major system change on data that cannot be verified through audit creates data integrity risk that could persist into future years. A lender or peer council needs assurance that the migration was sound; the fact it was not audited represents a control gap at a critical time.
findings.figures: System migration occurred during 2022/23-2024/25 disclaimed periods
findings.quote: The Authority's change in its financial system which occurred during the period of disclaimed audit opinions. No external audit work was carried out on the migration of data to the new system. It is likely this risk will require additional audit procedures

findings.headline: Finance team departures without contingency arrangements delayed 2021/22 audit completion to 29 November 2023
findings.detail: Departures from the finance team hindered capacity and created delays in audit assistance, with no contingency arrangements in place to retain expertise or manage transition. This directly delayed finalisation of the 2021/22 accounts (published 29 July 2022, audit completed 29 November 2023). The auditors identified this as a significant weakness in governance and financial reporting arrangements, with recommendations to ensure adequate team capacity and capability.
findings.matters: Turnover in core finance functions without succession planning or business continuity is a governance failure. A peer council or lender assessing institutional resilience would see this as evidence the Authority lacks structural safeguards to maintain continuity through staffing changes.
findings.figures: Departures between 2021/22 and 2023/24; 2021/22 audit span from 29 July 2022 draft to 29 November 2023 final
findings.quote: Departures from the Authority's finance team hindered the Authority's capacity to assist the audit process. The authority did not have contingency arrangements in place to address the loss of expertise, leading to delays addressing audit queries and finalising the financial statements

findings.headline: Bank reconciliation process failed to properly reconcile to general ledger in 2024/25.
findings.detail: The Authority completed monthly bank reconciliations throughout 2024/25 but identified after year-end that the process had not properly reconciled the bank balance to the general ledger. The auditors classified this as a significant weakness in governance. Recommendations include establishing robust processes, clearing the backlog, and providing staff training. Bank reconciliation is a fundamental control for financial management.
findings.matters: Bank reconciliation is a basic, non-delegable financial control. Failure to properly execute it signals either weak control design or weak operational discipline—both serious red flags for stakeholders assessing financial reporting reliability and cash management.
findings.figures: 2024/25 financial year; backlog of bank reconciliations noted
findings.quote: The Authority completed monthly bank reconciliations through 2024/25 but identified after the year-end that the process followed had not properly reconciled the bank balance to the Authority's general ledger. The bank reconciliation is a fundamental basis for the effective operation of financial controls

findings.headline: Material discrepancies identified in Movement in Reserves Statements for 2023/24 would have triggered audit qualification.
findings.detail: During the 2023/24 audit, the auditors identified material discrepancies between the Group and single entity Movement in Reserves Statements and entries elsewhere in the financial statements. This would have required a modification to the audit opinion had the backstop arrangements not applied. The issue goes to the integrity of reserves reporting, a fundamental indicator of financial position.
findings.matters: Material discrepancies in reserves statements mean the published financial position cannot be relied upon. A finance director, lender, or peer council needs assurance that reserves data is accurate as it directly affects understanding of the Authority's financial sustainability.
findings.figures: 2023/24 accounts, opinion date 26 February 2025
findings.quote: we identified material discrepancies between entries in both the Group and the single entity Movement in Reserves Statements and relevant entries presented elsewhere in the financial statements. This matter would have required a modification to our opinion on the financial statements in the absence of the backstop arrangements

findings.headline: Authority has received three consecutive disclaimed audit opinions and faces a fourth for 2025/26, with clean opinion not expected until 2027/28.
findings.detail: West Yorkshire Combined Authority received disclaimed opinions for 2022/23, 2023/24, and 2024/25. A disclaimer is the 'most likely outcome' for 2025/26 as well. Even with successful completion of current risk assessment work, the projected timeline shows 2026/27 will also be disclaimed (lack of assurance over opening reserves); only 2027/28 is projected to be qualified, still not clean. This represents five years without an unmodified opinion.
findings.matters: Multiple consecutive years without clean audit opinions indicates serious financial reporting and control capability issues. A lender or peer council watching this would see fundamental problems requiring substantial remediation work.
findings.figures: Disclaimer issued 6 December 2024 (2022/23); 26 February 2025 (2023/24); 26 February 2026 (2024/25). Opinions projected: 30 January 2027 (2025/26 disclaimed); 30 November 2027 (2026/27 disclaimed); 30 November 2028 (2027/28 qualified).
findings.quote: On 26 February 2026, we disclaimed our opinion on the Authority's 2024/25 financial statements. This followed on from disclaimed opinions issued previously in respect of the Authority's 2023/2024 accounts.

findings.headline: Combined Authority and Police authority maintain under-borrowed position, with proportion of capital financing requirement funded from cash balances and reserves rather than external borrowing
findings.detail: Both organisations continue to fund part of their underlying capital financing requirement from cash balances and reserves rather than taking external borrowing. Council assesses this approach as appropriate while cash balances remain strong and PWLB borrowing rates remain comparatively high, reducing short-term borrowing costs.
findings.matters: Reflects deliberate financing strategy balancing borrowing costs against rates available; position is dependent on maintaining strong cash balances and PWLB rates remaining at current levels; affects future borrowing capacity
findings.figures: None specific to this position
findings.quote: Both the Combined Authority and WYP continue to maintain an under-borrowed position. This means that a proportion of the underlying capital financing requirement is currently being funded from cash balances and reserves rather than external borrowing. This approach reduces borrowing costs in the short term and remains appropriate while cash balances are strong and PWLB borrowing rates remain comparatively high.

findings.headline: West Yorkshire's investment portfolio achieved 4.16% weighted average rate of return in Q1, outperforming both local authority peer group (4.10%) and metropolitan district average (3.93%)
findings.detail: Treasury management performance exceeded both comparator groups. Portfolio also achieved lowest weighted average credit risk score (1.22 compared to peer group 1.63 and metropolitan districts 1.44) while maintaining longer investment durations. Demonstrates higher returns achieved without increased overall portfolio risk.
findings.matters: Shows effective treasury management and cash deployment; rate of return directly affects council's financial position and is relevant comparison point for other councils' treasury practice
findings.figures: WARoR: 4.16% (WYCA), 4.10% (peer group), 3.93% (metropolitan districts); credit risk: 1.22 (WYCA), 1.63 (peer group), 1.44 (metro districts)
findings.quote: the Authority achieved a weighted average rate of return of 4.16%, outperforming both the benchmarking group (4.10%) and metropolitan district average (3.93%). While maintaining longer investment durations, the Authority also reported the lowest weighted average credit risk score, demonstrating that higher returns have been achieved without increasing overall portfolio risk.

findings.headline: Council initiating review of cashflow forecasting arrangements and investment strategy following need for short-term borrowing, with focus on liquidity management ahead of anticipated property transactions
findings.detail: In response to the short-term borrowing requirement, a review is underway to assess accuracy of forecast cash movements and ensure appropriate liquidity is maintained through instant-access investments. Review is considered particularly important given council's expectation of significant property-related transactions during the remainder of 2026/27, which will increase need for readily available funds.
findings.matters: Signals prior cashflow forecasting was inadequate; demonstrates governance response to identified issue; property transaction activity suggests capital expenditure programme ahead
findings.figures: None specific
findings.quote: In response, a review is being carried out of both the Authority's cashflow forecasting arrangements and its underlying investment strategy. The review will assess the accuracy of forecast cash movements and ensure that an appropriate level of liquidity is maintained through instant-access investments. This is particularly important as the Authority enters a period in which significant property-related transactions may occur, increasing the need for readily available funds and placing greater emphasis on effective liquidity management.

findings.headline: Net investments increased by £464m in Q1 following implementation of Integrated Settlement funding arrangements that deliver funding upfront rather than in instalments
findings.detail: Group net investments grew from £567m to £1,031m in Q1. Funds are received at the start of the financial year under the new Integrated Settlement arrangements and are being held temporarily pending their application to approved programmes as expenditure is incurred through the year. This has resulted in significantly higher cash balances.
findings.matters: Finance directors track cash position and liquidity; this shows strong cash balances creating both opportunity and management complexity that the council is addressing through strategy review
findings.figures: £464m increase; £567.189m to £1,030.834m (Group Net Investments)
findings.quote: Net investments increased by £464 million during Quarter 1. This largely reflects the implementation of Integrated Settlement funding arrangements, under which funding is received at the start of the financial year rather than in instalments throughout the year.

findings.paper_title: Item 11- Appendix 1 - Audit Recommendation Follow Up Report
findings.headline: Three audit recommendations formally not agreed by management, signalling governance disagreement
findings.detail: The People and Transformation directorate did not accept three recommendations: (1) monthly budget reporting to DOBs; (2) annual Declaration of Interest forms for contract managers; (3) formal documented assessment of project assurance exemptions. Audit has rebutted management responses, particularly on budget reporting and project assurance documentation, noting that other directorates facing similar resource constraints have accepted comparable recommendations.
findings.matters: When management formally rejects audit recommendations on governance matters, it signals potential disagreement over control standards and accountability. For a lender, this raises questions about the organisation's commitment to embedding audit findings and whether governance gaps will persist.
findings.figures: 3 recommendations not agreed; primarily from People and Transformation directorate
findings.quote: This recommendation has been reflected across a number of directorates, as a result the Senior Leadership Team have taken a more consistent and collaborative organisation wide approach where necessary actions will be led by the Finance and Commercial Director.

findings.paper_title: Item 11- Appendix 1 - Audit Recommendation Follow Up Report
findings.headline: Finance representation absent from directorate oversight boards, creating governance gaps in budget accountability
findings.detail: The report notes that in People and Transformation, four consecutive directorate outcome board (DOB) meetings took place without finance representation. Financial updates were provided verbally rather than through formal documented reports. The audit stated this lacks independent financial challenge, transparency, and audit trail compared to Finance-led reporting. The directorate did not formally accept this recommendation, citing finance resource constraints.
findings.matters: Missing finance representation at board-level governance diminishes financial oversight and accountability. For a lender, this indicates a control gap in budget scrutiny and financial stewardship at directorate level.
findings.figures: Four consecutive DOB meetings without finance representation
findings.quote: four consecutive DOB meetings took place without finance representation, and financial updates were provided verbally rather than through documented reports prepared by Finance. Whilst alternative budget monitoring arrangements were in place and provided a degree of financial oversight, they did not offer the same level of independent financial challenge, transparency, assurance, and audit trail

findings.paper_title: Item 11- Appendix 1 - Audit Recommendation Follow Up Report
findings.headline: Finance team capacity constraints are delaying implementation of debt management and financial control recommendations
findings.detail: Recommendations 64–67 (debt management policy and processes) are delayed due to long-term absence of the substantive risk owner. The report notes that a Financial Controller is due to start on 12 October and will assume responsibility for these actions. Until then, debt policy updates have been deprioritised.
findings.matters: Finance team resourcing directly affects the pace of financial control improvement. A new Financial Controller starting mid-October means there will be a transition period. For a lender assessing financial governance, understaffing in core finance roles is a risk signal.
findings.figures: Start date for new Financial Controller: 12 October 2026
findings.quote: Ongoing sickness of the substantive risk owner has led to redistribution of tasks and prioritisation, and update of the debt policy has been deemed a lower priority than other items. Financial Controller (FC) is due to start on 12 October and will take on

findings.paper_title: Item 11- Appendix 1 - Audit Recommendation Follow Up Report
findings.headline: Risk management framework implementation pushed to end of 2027 and March 2028, extending from original 2026 dates
findings.detail: Recommendation 49 (condensed risk register template) has been extended to 31 December 2027; Recommendation 50 (automated risk reporting via Power BI) has been extended to 31 March 2028. Both delays are attributed to interdependencies: the automated solution cannot be built until the template is tested and approved.
findings.matters: A functioning risk management framework is foundational to council governance and internal control. Delays of 12–18 months beyond original timelines mean governance weaknesses across the organisation remain unaddressed for an extended period.
findings.figures: Original dates: Rec 49 was due 30 September 2026 (now 31 December 2027); Rec 50 was due 31 March 2027 (now 31 March 2028)
findings.quote: A revised implementation date should be applied of 31/12/2027... As the revised template remains in testing and has not yet been approved for organisational rollout, developing Power App functionality using the current template risks duplication and rework. A revised implementation date of 31 March 2028 would allow sufficient time

findings.paper_title: Item 11- Appendix 1 - Audit Recommendation Follow Up Report
findings.headline: Multiple financial control recommendations for transport services remain overdue or incomplete
findings.detail: Recommendations 21–25 cover financial controls in tendered bus services, including budget setting processes, contract management, and the Deloitte financial model implementation. Several actions are overdue or require further assurance through walkthrough reviews that have not yet been scheduled or completed.
findings.matters: Financial controls in a major revenue-generating service (bus operations) are not fully embedded. For a lender, unresolved financial control weaknesses in a significant service line signal risk to the council's financial stewardship and revenue management.
findings.figures: Recommendations 21–25; several marked as overdue or awaiting completion of verification steps
findings.quote: Internal Audit is currently liaising with the Head of Passenger Experience to schedule this review.

findings.paper_title: Item 11- Appendix 1 - Audit Recommendation Follow Up Report
findings.headline: 27 of 91 outstanding audit recommendations are overdue, many by six months or more
findings.detail: The report tracks 91 audit actions across the authority. The performance metrics show 46 on track, 18 with revised dates or concerns about delivery, and 27 overdue. The aged analysis chart shows material portions of actions overdue by 6–9 months, 9–12 months, over 12 months, and over 24 months.
findings.matters: Overdue audit recommendations indicate control weaknesses and governance gaps are not being remediated at pace. A lender needs to know whether identified control issues are being fixed or accumulating.
findings.figures: 27 overdue out of 91 outstanding (29.7%); 46 on track; 18 with revised dates or concerns
findings.quote: Key: 46 On track, no issues identified at this stage. 18 Revised date or concerns about ability to achieve due date 27 Overdue

findings.paper_title: 11. Quarterly Audit Recommendation Follow Up Report
findings.headline: Audit recommendations from Climate Emergency Plan not yet tracked for implementation
findings.detail: The council has completed its Climate and Environment Plan review but has not yet undertaken a follow-up on the resulting audit recommendations. The council explicitly notes that delayed implementation would carry delivery risk for the organisation.
findings.matters: Untracked implementation of strategic recommendations represents unmanaged delivery risk; finance directors and peer councils monitor whether organizations can execute on major commitments.
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: A report on Climate and Environment Plan was recently completed so while there has not yet been a follow up on the recommendations from that review, if these are not actioned in a timely way, this will carry a delivery risk for the organisation.

findings.paper_title: 11. Quarterly Audit Recommendation Follow Up Report
findings.headline: Increase in older outstanding audit recommendations despite overall fall in total numbers
findings.detail: The council reports that while total outstanding recommendations have decreased, the proportion of older recommendations has increased. The paper identifies as a key risk that recommendations are taking longer to deliver than is appropriate, which could delay remediation of identified control weaknesses.
findings.matters: Finance directors and lenders assess audit follow-up pace as a measure of governance quality and control implementation effectiveness; accumulation of overdue recommendations suggests potential implementation challenges.
findings.figures: No figures provided in main report; detail in Appendix 1
findings.quote: While the overall number of recommendations have gone down, there has been an increase in the number of older recommendations

findings.headline: Counter-fraud investigation identified time recording and purchase card control concerns in human resources
findings.detail: The most significant audit findings are HR time recording issues including polygamous working and purchase card policy breaches. The council has made recommendations to strengthen the time recording system and purchase card policy compliance.
findings.matters: Payroll and purchase card controls are material for financial management; control weaknesses in these areas directly affect the council's control environment
findings.figures: None provided
findings.quote: The most significant areas that are being reported are those Human Resources activities in relation to time recording/polygamous working and purchase card concerns. Recommendations have been made to strengthen these areas with a push to improve the time recording system and compliance with purchase card policies.

findings.headline: Internal audit plan delivery at 20% against 30% September target, 50% January target at risk
findings.detail: Staffing absences and time to fill vacancies have caused the shortfall. Although 43% of work is underway or completed, achieving the January target is uncertain despite efforts being made.
findings.matters: An internal audit function falling behind its plan raises the risk that control weaknesses in the council will not be identified and remedied in a timely way
findings.figures: 30% target by end of September, 20% actual delivery, 50% target by end of January, 43% of work underway or completed
findings.quote: The target of completing 30% delivery of the plan by the end of September is unlikely to be achieved, predominantly because of some staffing absences in the team and the length of time it has taken to fill remaining vacancies. Current delivery is at 20% based on finalised and draft reports. The target of 50% delivery by the end of January is therefore also at risk at this point, but given that 43% of work is already underway or completed, every effort will be made to achieve our remaining targets.

findings.headline: Medium Term Financial Strategy under review to reflect July government devolution announcements, Integrated Settlement, and expanded authority responsibilities, with detailed proposals due to board in December.
findings.detail: The authority is revising its MTFS and developing the 2027-28 budget to align with devolution changes and expanded responsibilities. A revised Reserves Strategy will be developed alongside the MTFS. The detailed MTFS report and 2027-28 budget proposals are scheduled for December 2026.
findings.matters: MTFS revision triggered by devolution and new funding settlement signals potential structural changes to the financial model. For a lender, this indicates current planning assumptions may require adjustment and there is material uncertainty pending the December outcome.
findings.figures: Detailed report and budget proposals expected December 2026
findings.quote: The West Yorkshire Combined Authority is reviewing its medium term financial strategy and plan to take account of the opportunities presented by devolution including the announcements made by HMG in July, the Integrated Settlement and the Authority's expanding responsibilities.

findings.headline: General Fund Reserves forecast to reduce from £157.8m to £149.9m by year-end, drawn to support bus franchising transition and manage transitional pressures.
findings.detail: Reserves are being drawn down approximately £7.9m in 2026-27, with a further £6.5m planned transfer to earmarked reserves. This drawdown is structured to support strategic priorities, specifically the bus franchising transition programme.
findings.matters: Reserve depletion rate and resulting level affect the authority's financial resilience and capacity to absorb unexpected shocks. For a lender, the £149.9m reserve floor and planned drawdown pattern are factors in assessing credit strength and sustainability.
findings.figures: £157.8m down to £149.9m (£7.9m reduction); £6.5m transfer to earmarked reserves
findings.quote: General Fund Reserves are forecast to reduce from £157.8m to £149.9m by 31 March 2027, reflecting planned drawdowns to support strategic priorities and manage transitional pressures.

findings.headline: Revenue and capital delivery concentrated in latter half of financial year, with capital programme only 13.5% delivered by end of Q1, requiring close monitoring of milestones and grant claims.
findings.detail: Year-to-date through June shows £33.7m income below profile and £20.6m expenditure below profile in revenue, while capital delivery stands at only 13.5% of the rebased budget. Both reflect timing of programme milestones and grant claim profiles, with significant delivery expected in final months.
findings.matters: Back-loaded delivery creates execution risk: non-delivery of final-quarter commitments, grant claim rejections, or unexpected year-end adjustments. This concentration affects forecast reliability and is a classic timing risk for authorities managing complex programmes.
findings.figures: YTD net variance £13.1m (£33.7m income below, £20.6m expenditure below profile); Q1 capital delivery 13.5% of £576.8m budget; forecast year-end 94.1% delivered
findings.quote: The scale of current timing variances highlights a continued reliance on the delivery of programmes in the latter part of the financial year. As such, close monitoring of project milestones, expenditure profiles and grant drawdown will be required throughout the year.

findings.headline: Transport directorate facing emerging pressures of £0.9m on Concessionary Travel and £5.8m on Tendered Services, currently offset by external grant funding but flagged for continued monitoring.
findings.detail: Transport Services has identified £6.7m in emerging cost pressures across two core service areas. These are currently being covered by external grant funding, but the paper's emphasis on monitoring suggests uncertainty about future grant persistence or whether these pressures will grow.
findings.matters: Concessionary travel and tendered services are statutory transport functions. Emerging pressures suggest operational cost inflation or demand changes that grants may not cover long-term. For a lender, this signals potential future revenue pressure points on a core service.
findings.figures: £0.9m Concessionary Travel; £5.8m Tendered Services; total £6.7m emerging pressures
findings.quote: However, Transport Services faces emerging pressures of £0.9m on Concessionary Travel and £5.8m on Tendered Services, these are currently being offset by external grant funding and will continue to be monitored.

findings.headline: Zero Emission Bus programme delayed to 2027-28, creating £38.4m variance to Bus and Customer Offer budget—the largest single capital variance.
findings.detail: Revised delivery timescales mean Zero Emission Bus expenditure is now expected to fall in 2027-28 rather than 2026-27. This single variance accounts for most of the overall capital programme's £33.4m forecast underspend and directly impacts bus franchising transition plans.
findings.matters: Bus franchising is a strategic priority supported by reserve drawdown. Delays to zero emission bus investment signal execution constraints on a high-profile environmental commitment. For a lender, this indicates delivery risk on core transition programmes.
findings.figures: £38.4m below rebased budget; represents 115% of total £33.4m capital underspend
findings.quote: The principal variance relates to the Bus and Customer Offer programme, where forecast expenditure is £38.4m below the rebased budget. This is primarily due to revised delivery timescales for the Zero Emission Bus programme, with expenditure now expected to fall in 2027/28.

findings.headline: Capital programme rebased down from £767.2m to £576.8m (24.8% reduction), reflecting revised delivery schedules following government confirmation that expenditure can extend beyond programme end date.
findings.detail: The January 2026 approved capital budget was reduced significantly to align with government confirmation that funding commitments must be made by March 2027 but delivery and expenditure can extend beyond. The rebasing also reflects scheme prioritization work focusing on schemes most advanced in development and best positioned to deliver outcomes.
findings.matters: A 24.8% reduction on a £767m programme signals either planning challenges when the budget was set or material external constraint changes. For a lender, this raises questions about capital forecasting confidence and whether this adjustment will recur in future years.
findings.figures: £767.2m original approved budget; £576.8m rebased budget; Q1 delivery £77.8m (13.5% of rebased); forecast year-end £543.4m
findings.quote: The 2026/27 Capital Programme has been rebased from the Combined Authority approved budget of £767.2m to £576.8m, a 24.8% reduction this in line with 2025/26 outturn position, together with confirmed funding allocations, revised delivery schedules and updated programme assumptions.

news_drafts.headline: West Yorkshire Combined Authority and Police fund part of their borrowing need from own cash, not loans
news_drafts.lead:
West Yorkshire Combined Authority, the body run by the region's councils for transport and economic growth, and West Yorkshire Police are both paying for part of their long-term spending from their own cash rather than from loans. The first-quarter treasury management update (how a body borrows, invests spare cash and manages the risks of both) goes to the Governance & Audit Committee on 8 October 2026.

The update says both continue to hold an "under-borrowed" position. Each has a capital financing requirement (CFR), the total spent on long-lived assets that has not yet been paid for, in effect its underlying need to borrow. A proportion of that is being met from cash balances and reserves, money set aside, rather than external borrowing. This is known as internal borrowing, which saves interest but uses up the cushion.

The paper says the approach reduces borrowing costs in the short term and "remains appropriate while cash balances are strong and PWLB borrowing rates remain comparatively high". The PWLB, the Public Works Loan Board, is the government's lending arm for councils and where most council borrowing comes from. The paper gives no figure for the share funded from cash.
